ab_wheel.what: Kneeling, you roll a small wheel out in front of you and pull it back. It is a hard exercise for the whole front of your stomach.
ab_wheel.find: A small wheel with a handle on each side. Use a mat under your knees.
setup: Kneel on a mat and hold the handles with the wheel under your shoulders.
Tuck your hips under and tighten your stomach.
do: Roll the wheel forward slowly, hips and arms opening together.
Go only as far as you can without your lower back sagging.
Pull the wheel back toward your knees using your abs.
ab_wheel.feel: The whole front of your stomach, plus the sides of your back.
avoid: Lower back sagging. Shorten the roll and keep your hips tucked.
Pulling back with the hips first. Keep hips and arms moving together.

video.title: Ab Wheel- How to PROPERLY Use an Ab Wheel | MIND PUMP

arnold_press.what: A dumbbell shoulder press that starts with palms facing you and turns as you press. It works the whole shoulder.
arnold_press.find: Bench with an upright backrest and two dumbbells, lighter than your normal press.
setup: Sit with your back against the pad and feet flat.
Hold the dumbbells in front of your shoulders, palms facing you.
do: Press up while turning your palms to face forward.
Finish with arms straight overhead, palms forward.
Reverse the turn as you lower, back to palms facing you.
arnold_press.feel: Front and side of the shoulders, plus the back of the upper arms.
avoid: Rushing the turn. Rotate smoothly through the whole press.
Arching off the backrest. Keep your ribs down.

video.title: Arnold Press - Shoulder Exercise - Proper Form Tutorial

assisted_pull_up.what: A pull-up on a machine that helps push you up with a counterweight. It builds your back and arms until you can do full pull-ups.
assisted_pull_up.find: Tall machine with pull-up handles on top, a weight stack and a pad for your knees or feet.
setup: Set the pin. More weight means more help, so start heavy.
Grip the top handles a bit wider than your shoulders, palms facing away.
Kneel or step onto the pad and let your arms go straight.
do: Pull your shoulders down away from your ears first.
Drive your elbows down to your sides until your chin is over the handles.
Lower slowly, 2 to 3 seconds, until your arms are straight again.
assisted_pull_up.feel: The sides of your back under the armpits, plus the front of your upper arms.
avoid: Bouncing off the pad. Pause at the bottom and pull smoothly.
Jumping off at the end. Hold the handles and let the pad rise slowly.

video.title: How To PROPERLY Use The Assisted Pull Up Machine (DO MORE PULL UPS)

back_extension.what: You fold forward over a pad at the hips and lift your body back up. It strengthens your lower back, glutes and hamstrings.
back_extension.find: Angled bench with a thigh pad and ankle rollers. Also called hyperextension bench or Roman chair.
setup: Set the pad just below your hip crease so you can fold freely at the hips.
Hook your heels under the rollers and cross your arms over your chest.
do: Keep your back flat and fold forward at the hips until your hamstrings stretch.
Squeeze your glutes and lift until your body is one straight line.
Pause for a second there, then lower slowly.
back_extension.feel: Glutes, back of the thighs and the muscles along your lower spine.
avoid: Arching up past straight. Stop when your body forms a straight line.
Rounding and jerking up. Move slowly with a flat back.

video.title: STOP Doing Back Extensions Like This!

back_squat.what: A squat with a barbell resting across your upper back. It is the main lift for strong legs, glutes and a stiff trunk.
back_squat.find: Squat rack or power rack with a barbell on hooks and safety bars at the sides.
setup: Set the hooks at upper chest height and the safety bars just below squat depth.
Duck under and rest the bar on your upper back muscles, not on your neck.
Stand up, take two steps back. Feet shoulder width, toes slightly out.
do: Take a big breath into your belly and tighten your stomach.
Sit down between your hips, knees following the line of your toes.
Go down until your thighs are about level with the floor, back flat.
Push the floor away with your whole foot and stand up tall.
back_squat.feel: Front of the thighs and glutes. Your stomach and back work to keep you stiff.
avoid: Knees caving inward. Push them out so they stay over your toes.
Heels lifting or chest dropping. Keep the whole foot down and chest up.

video.title: How to Perform the Squat - Proper Squats Form & Technique

barbell_row.what: Bent over with a flat back, you pull a barbell up to your stomach. It builds the whole back.
barbell_row.find: A barbell on the floor or in a rack at knee height.
setup: Grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders, palms facing your legs.
Push your hips back and lean forward until your back is close to level.
Knees slightly bent, back flat, arms hanging straight.
do: Pull the bar to your belly button, elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight. Keep your upper body still.
barbell_row.feel: Middle and sides of the back. Lower back and hamstrings hold the position.
avoid: Standing up more with each rep. Hold the same lean and go lighter.
Rounding your back. Keep your chest proud and back flat.

video.title: How To: Barbell Bent-Over Row

bench_press.what: You lie on a bench and press a barbell up from your chest. It is the main lift for chest, front shoulders and triceps.
bench_press.find: Flat bench with a barbell on uprights above your head. Use safety arms or ask someone to spot you.
setup: Lie down with your eyes under the bar and your feet flat on the floor.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and keep them pinned to the bench.
Grip a little wider than shoulder width, thumbs wrapped around the bar.
do: Lift the bar out and bring it over your shoulders with straight arms.
Lower it slowly to mid chest, elbows about 45 degrees out from your sides.
Touch lightly, then press up until your arms are straight.
bench_press.feel: Chest, front of the shoulders and back of the upper arms.
avoid: Bouncing the bar off your chest. Touch lightly, then press.
Elbows flared straight out. Tuck them to about 45 degrees.

video.title: How To: Barbell Bench Press

biceps_curl.what: You bend your elbows to lift dumbbells toward your shoulders. It is direct work for the biceps on the front of your upper arms.
biceps_curl.find: Dumbbell rack. Pick a pair you can curl without swinging your body.
setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight, palms facing forward.
Pin your elbows to your sides and tighten your stomach.
do: Curl both dumbbells up until they are close to your shoulders.
Squeeze for a second at the top.
Lower slowly, 2 to 3 seconds, until your arms are fully straight.
avoid: Swinging your back to lift. Go lighter and keep your body still.
Elbows drifting forward. Keep them by your ribs.

video.title: How to Do a Dumbbell Biceps Curl | Arm Workout

bulgarian_split_squat.what: A one leg squat with your back foot resting on a bench. It builds each leg on its own and trains your balance.
bulgarian_split_squat.find: A flat bench or knee high box and two dumbbells. Leave free space in front of the bench.
setup: Stand one big step in front of the bench, a dumbbell in each hand.
Reach one foot back and rest the top of it on the bench.
Front foot flat, far enough forward that the heel stays down at the bottom.
do: Lower straight down until your front thigh is about level with the floor.
Lean your chest slightly forward and keep the front knee over your toes.
Push through the whole front foot to stand up.
Finish all reps on one leg, then switch.
bulgarian_split_squat.feel: Front thigh and glute of the front leg. A stretch in the hip of the back leg.
avoid: Pushing off the back foot. Let it rest and make the front leg work.
Standing too close to the bench. Step out until your front heel stays down.

video.title: How To: Bulgarian Split Squat

cable_biceps_curl.what: A biceps curl with a cable instead of dumbbells. The cable keeps your biceps working through the whole movement.
cable_biceps_curl.find: Cable tower with the pulley at the bottom and a short straight or zigzag bar attached.
setup: Slide the pulley to the lowest position and clip on a short bar.
Grip the bar palms up, hands shoulder width, and take a small step back.
Stand tall with your arms straight and elbows by your sides.
do: Curl the bar up toward your shoulders without moving your upper arms.
Squeeze for a second at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight again.
cable_biceps_curl.feel: Front of the upper arms, all the way up and all the way down.
avoid: Leaning back to pull the weight. Stay upright and go lighter.
Elbows sliding forward. Keep them pinned to your ribs.

video.title: How to PROPERLY Cable Bicep Curl For Bigger Biceps (EASY FIX)

cable_crunch.what: A kneeling crunch against a cable. It lets you add weight to ab training so your abs keep getting stronger.
cable_crunch.find: Cable tower with the pulley at the top and a rope handle. Put a mat under your knees.
setup: Set the pulley high and clip on the rope.
Kneel facing the tower and hold the rope ends beside your head.
Keep your hips up above your knees. Do not sit back on your heels.
do: Curl your chest down toward your knees by rounding your back.
Bring your elbows toward your thighs and squeeze your abs hard.
Uncurl slowly until your back is straight. Your hips stay still.
cable_crunch.feel: The front of your stomach. Not your arms or hips.
avoid: Pulling with your arms. Lock your hands by your head and move only your spine.
Rocking your hips back. Keep them fixed above your knees.

video.title: How to PROPERLY Cable Crunch to Shape Your Abs (How to Kneeling Cable Abdominal Crunch)

cable_fly.what: Standing between two cables, you bring your hands together in front of you in a wide hugging arc. It isolates the chest.
cable_fly.find: Double cable station, two towers facing each other, with a single handle on each side.
setup: Set both pulleys above shoulder height and clip on single handles.
Grab one handle, then the other, and step forward, one foot in front.
Lean slightly forward, arms out wide, elbows slightly bent.
do: Sweep your hands down and together in front of your lower chest.
Squeeze your chest for a second as your hands meet.
Open slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest.
cable_fly.feel: Across the chest, most when your hands meet.
avoid: Bending and straightening the elbows like a press. Keep one fixed slight bend.
Arms going far behind you. Stop when your hands are level with your chest.

video.title: How To: High Cable Chest Fly

cable_lateral_raise.what: You lift one arm out to the side against a low cable. It builds the side of the shoulder with steady resistance.
cable_lateral_raise.find: Cable tower with the pulley at the bottom and a single D shaped handle.
setup: Set the pulley to the lowest position and clip on a single handle.
Stand side on to the tower and hold the handle in the hand furthest from it.
Hold the tower with your free hand. The cable crosses in front of your body.
do: With a slightly bent elbow, lift your arm out to the side.
Stop when your hand is level with your shoulder.
Lower slowly, 2 to 3 seconds. Finish all reps, then switch sides.
cable_lateral_raise.feel: The outside of the shoulder on the working arm.
avoid: Shrugging the shoulder up to your ear. Keep it down and lift with the arm.
Jerking the weight up. Go light and lift smoothly.

video.title: How to PROPERLY Cable Lateral Raise (TRY THIS!)

cable_overhead_triceps_extension.what: Facing away from a cable, you straighten your arms overhead with a rope. It trains the triceps from a deep stretch.
cable_overhead_triceps_extension.find: Cable tower with a rope handle, pulley set at the bottom.
setup: Set the pulley at the bottom and clip on the rope.
Hold the rope with both hands, turn away and lift it behind your head.
Step forward, one foot in front, elbows pointing up beside your head.
do: Straighten your arms until your hands are above your head.
Keep your upper arms still. Only your forearms move.
Lower the rope slowly behind your head until you feel a deep stretch.
cable_overhead_triceps_extension.feel: Back of the upper arms, with a deep stretch at the bottom.
avoid: Elbows flaring wide. Keep them close to your head.
Arching your back. Tighten your stomach and keep your ribs down.

video.title: How to PROPERLY Overhead Cable Tricep Extension | Fix Your Tricep Extension Form NOW!

cable_row_single_arm.what: A seated cable row done with one arm at a time. It lets each side of your back work on its own.
cable_row_single_arm.find: Low cable row station with a bench seat and foot plates. Swap to a single D shaped handle.
setup: Clip a single handle to the low cable and sit with your feet on the plates.
Grip the handle in one hand and slide back until your arm is straight.
Sit tall with your chest up. Rest the free hand on your thigh.
do: Pull the handle to the side of your waist, elbow close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blade back for a second.
Return slowly until your arm is straight.
Finish all reps, then switch arms.
cable_row_single_arm.feel: The side and middle of your back on the working side.
avoid: Twisting your upper body to pull further. Keep your chest facing the stack.
Leaning back. Stay upright and let your back do the pulling.

video.title: Single Arm Seated Cable Row | How To Perform It Correctly

chest_supported_row.what: You lie chest down on an incline bench and row two dumbbells. It trains your upper back without loading your lower back.
chest_supported_row.find: Adjustable bench set to a low incline, about 30 to 45 degrees, and two dumbbells.
setup: Set the bench to 30 to 45 degrees and put the dumbbells at the head end.
Lie face down with your chest at the top of the pad, feet on the floor.
Let the dumbbells hang straight down, palms facing each other.
do: Pull your elbows back toward your hips until the dumbbells reach your ribs.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for a second.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
chest_supported_row.feel: Middle of your back, between and below the shoulder blades.
avoid: Lifting your chest off the pad. Keep it glued down and go lighter.
Shrugging up toward your ears. Pull your elbows back and down.

video.title: How to PROPERLY Incline Dumbbell Row (CHEST SUPPORTED ROW DONE RIGHT)

chest_supported_t_bar_row.what: Lying chest down on an angled pad, you pull a loaded lever up toward you. It builds the back without loading your lower back.
chest_supported_t_bar_row.find: Angled machine with a chest pad, a foot plate and a lever arm you load with plates.
setup: Adjust the foot plate so the top of the pad sits at your upper chest.
Load the plates, lie chest down and grip the handles.
Lift the lever off its rest and let your arms hang straight.
do: Pull the handles up toward your lower chest, elbows going back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for a second.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
chest_supported_t_bar_row.feel: Middle of the back and between the shoulder blades.
avoid: Chest lifting off the pad. Stay glued to it and use less weight.
Cutting the bottom short. Let your arms go fully straight on each rep.

video.title: Exercise Tutorial - Chest Supported T-Bar Row

chin_up.what: A pull-up with your palms facing you. It builds the back and puts more work on the biceps.
chin_up.find: A pull-up bar. Use a box or step to reach it if needed.
setup: Grip the bar at shoulder width with your palms facing you.
Hang with straight arms and keep your legs still.
do: Pull your shoulders down, then pull your chest up toward the bar.
Keep going until your chin is over the bar.
Lower slowly to fully straight arms.
chin_up.feel: Front of the upper arms and the sides of your back.
avoid: Craning your neck to reach the bar. Pull your chest up to it.
Swinging your legs. Tighten your stomach and stay still.

video.title: Proper Chin-Up Form

conventional_deadlift.what: You lift a loaded barbell from the floor to standing. It trains the whole back side of your body and your grip.
conventional_deadlift.find: A barbell with full size plates on the floor, on a lifting platform or rubber mats.
setup: Stand with feet hip width and the bar over the middle of your feet.
Bend down, grip the bar just outside your legs and bring your shins to it.
Lift your chest until your back is flat. Pull up on the bar until it feels tight.
do: Take a big breath and tighten your stomach.
Push the floor away and stand up, keeping the bar against your legs.
Stand tall at the top. Do not lean back.
To lower, push your hips back, then bend your knees once the bar passes them.
conventional_deadlift.feel: Glutes, back of the thighs and your whole back. Your grip works hard too.
avoid: Rounding your back. Lift your chest and flatten it before the bar moves.
Jerking the bar. Squeeze it off the floor and keep it close to your legs.

video.title: Learning to Deadlift | The Starting Strength Method

dead_bug.what: Lying on your back, you slowly lower the opposite arm and leg. It teaches your abs to hold your lower back still.
dead_bug.find: A mat on the floor. No equipment needed.
setup: Lie on your back with your arms pointing straight up at the ceiling.
Lift your legs so your hips and knees are bent at 90 degrees.
Press your lower back gently into the floor.
do: Slowly lower your right arm overhead and your left leg toward the floor.
Stop just above the floor, or earlier if your lower back starts to lift.
Return to the start and repeat with the left arm and right leg.
Breathe out as you reach. Take about 3 seconds each way.
dead_bug.feel: Deep in your stomach muscles. Your lower back should stay relaxed.
avoid: Lower back arching off the floor. Shorten the reach until it stays down.
Rushing. Move slowly and keep the other arm and leg still.

video.title: How to Do a Dead Bug: A Guide from Physical Therapists

dips.what: Holding yourself up on two parallel bars, you lower your body by bending your elbows and press back up. It builds chest and triceps.
dips.find: Two parallel bars at about hip height, often part of a pull-up tower.
setup: Grip the bars and step or jump up so your straight arms hold your weight.
Pull your shoulders down away from your ears.
Bend your knees and lean your chest slightly forward.
do: Bend your elbows and lower slowly, elbows pointing back.
Stop when your upper arms are about level with the floor.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
dips.feel: Lower chest, back of the upper arms and front of the shoulders.
avoid: Dropping too deep. Stop when your upper arms are level with the floor.
Shoulders shrugging up to your ears. Keep them pressed down.

video.title: The Perfect Dip  - Do it right

dumbbell_bench_press.what: You lie on a flat bench and press two dumbbells up from your chest. It builds chest, shoulders and triceps, each side on its own.
dumbbell_bench_press.find: A flat bench and two dumbbells.
setup: Sit on the end of the bench with the dumbbells standing on your thighs.
Lie back and use your knees to help kick the dumbbells up to your chest.
Feet flat on the floor, shoulder blades squeezed together.
do: Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight over your chest.
Lower slowly until they are beside your chest, elbows about 45 degrees out.
Press back up, keeping your wrists straight above your elbows.
dumbbell_bench_press.feel: Chest, front of the shoulders and back of the upper arms.
avoid: Elbows flared straight out to the sides. Tuck them to about 45 degrees.
Dropping fast. Lower under control for about 2 seconds.

video.title: How To: Dumbbell Chest Press

dumbbell_fly.what: Lying on a bench, you open your arms wide with light dumbbells and bring them back together. It stretches and works the chest.
dumbbell_fly.find: A flat bench and two light dumbbells, much lighter than you press.
setup: Lie on the bench and press the dumbbells up over your chest, palms facing in.
Bend your elbows slightly and hold that angle.
Feet flat, shoulder blades squeezed together.
do: Open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc.
Stop when the dumbbells are level with your chest and you feel a stretch.
Bring them back together over your chest, like hugging a big tree.
dumbbell_fly.feel: A stretch across the chest at the bottom, a squeeze at the top.
avoid: Going too heavy or too deep. Use light weights and stop at chest level.
Locked straight arms. Keep a soft bend in your elbows.

video.title: How To: Dumbbell Flys On A Flat Bench

dumbbell_romanian_deadlift.what: Holding dumbbells, you push your hips back and lower the weights along your legs with a flat back. It trains hamstrings and glutes.
dumbbell_romanian_deadlift.find: Two dumbbells and a bit of open floor.
setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Feet hip width, knees slightly bent. Keep that small bend the whole time.
do: Hinge at the hips: push your butt straight back as if closing a door with it.
Slide the dumbbells down close to your legs, keeping your back flat.
Stop just below the knees or when the back of your thighs is fully stretched.
Squeeze your glutes and push your hips forward to stand up.
dumbbell_romanian_deadlift.feel: A strong stretch in the back of the thighs, then glutes as you stand.
avoid: Squatting down. Keep the knees soft and send your hips back.
Rounding your back to reach lower. Stop where your back stays flat.

video.title: Dumbbell Romanian (RDL) Deadlift |TECHNIQUE for Beginners

dumbbell_shoulder_press.what: Standing, you press two dumbbells from your shoulders to overhead. It builds shoulders and triceps and makes your trunk work.
dumbbell_shoulder_press.find: Two dumbbells and room to stand. A mirror helps.
setup: Bring the dumbbells up to shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Feet hip width. Squeeze your glutes and tighten your stomach.
Elbows slightly in front of your body, forearms upright.
do: Press both dumbbells straight up until your arms are straight.
Finish with your upper arms beside your ears.
Lower slowly back to shoulder height.
dumbbell_shoulder_press.feel: Shoulders and back of the upper arms. Stomach and glutes keep you steady.
avoid: Leaning back as you press. Squeeze glutes and abs so your ribs stay down.
Bouncing with your legs. Keep your knees still.

video.title: How to: Standing DB Shoulder Press for Physique Development

dumbbell_shrug.what: Holding heavy dumbbells, you lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears. It builds the muscles between neck and shoulders.
setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Arms straight, shoulders relaxed down.
do: Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as you can.
Pause for a second at the top.
Lower slowly all the way down.
dumbbell_shrug.feel: The top of the shoulders up to the neck.
avoid: Rolling your shoulders in circles. Move straight up and straight down.
Bending your elbows to help. Keep your arms long and relaxed.

video.title: How To: Dumbbell Shrugs

ez_bar_curl.what: A biceps curl with a short zigzag bar. The angled grips are more comfortable for the wrists than a straight bar.
ez_bar_curl.find: A short bar with a zigzag bend in the middle, called an EZ bar. Often on its own rack.
setup: Grip the angled parts of the bar at about shoulder width, palms up.
Stand tall with your arms straight and elbows by your sides.
do: Curl the bar up toward your shoulders without moving your elbows.
Squeeze for a second at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
avoid: Swinging your hips to start the rep. Stand still and go lighter.
Stopping short at the bottom. Straighten your arms fully on each rep.

video.title: How To EZ Bar Curl With Perfect Form (Grow Your Biceps)

face_pull.what: You pull a rope toward your face with your elbows high. It trains the back of the shoulders and the upper back.
face_pull.find: Cable tower with a rope handle, pulley set at about face height.
setup: Set the pulley at face height and clip on the rope.
Grip the rope ends with your thumbs pointing back toward you.
Step back until your arms are straight and the weight lifts off the stack.
do: Pull the rope toward your eyes with your elbows high and wide.
Pull the rope ends apart so your hands finish beside your ears.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then return slowly.
face_pull.feel: Back of the shoulders and between the shoulder blades.
avoid: Leaning back and heaving. Use a light weight and stand still.
Elbows dropping low. Keep them at shoulder height or higher.

video.title: How To Properly Perform Face Pulls For Rear Delts / Fix Your Form

farmers_carry.what: You walk while holding a heavy dumbbell in each hand. It builds grip, shoulders and a strong, steady trunk.
farmers_carry.find: Two heavy dumbbells or kettlebells and a clear lane of 10 to 20 metres.
setup: Stand between the dumbbells. Bend knees and hips to grip them, back flat.
Stand up tall. Shoulders back and down, chest up.
do: Walk with short, quick steps and look straight ahead.
Keep your body tall and the weights still at your sides.
At the end, bend your knees and set the weights down with a flat back.
farmers_carry.feel: Forearms and hands, upper back, and your stomach holding you tight.
avoid: Leaning or swaying. Go a little lighter and walk tall.
Shoulders creeping up to your ears. Pull them down and back.

video.title: How To Do The Farmers Walk Exercise PROPERLY (Step-By-Step Tutorial)

front_squat.what: A squat with the barbell resting on the front of your shoulders. It keeps you upright and puts more work on the front thighs.
front_squat.find: Squat rack with a barbell on hooks at upper chest height.
setup: Step in so the bar rests on the front of your shoulders, close to your throat.
Lift your elbows high in front, fingertips under the bar.
Stand up, step back. Feet shoulder width, toes slightly out.
do: Take a big breath and tighten your stomach.
Sit straight down with elbows high and chest up.
Go until your thighs are level with the floor or a little deeper.
Push through your whole foot to stand up.
front_squat.feel: Front of the thighs. Upper back and abs hold you upright.
avoid: Elbows dropping so the bar rolls forward. Drive them up the whole rep.
Holding the bar up with your hands. Let it sit on your shoulders.

video.title: How To Front Squat With Proper Form

glute_bridge.what: Lying on your back with knees bent, you lift your hips off the floor. It trains the glutes with no weight on your back.
glute_bridge.find: A mat on the floor. No equipment needed.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip width apart.
Heels about a hand length from your butt, arms by your sides.
do: Tighten your stomach and push through your heels to lift your hips.
Stop when knees, hips and shoulders form a straight line.
Squeeze your glutes for 1 to 2 seconds, then lower slowly.
glute_bridge.feel: Glutes, and a little in the back of the thighs.
avoid: Arching your lower back to get higher. Stop at a straight line and squeeze.
Pushing through your toes. Keep your weight in your heels.

video.title: How to Do a Glute Bridge Exercise: A Guide from Physical Therapists

goblet_squat.what: A squat holding one dumbbell against your chest. The weight in front makes it easy to stay upright and squat deep.
goblet_squat.find: One dumbbell or kettlebell. No rack needed.
setup: Hold one dumbbell upright against your chest, hands cupping the top end.
Feet shoulder width, toes turned slightly out.
Tuck your elbows in under the weight.
do: Sit straight down between your knees with your chest up.
Go as deep as you can with heels down and back flat.
Push through your whole foot to stand up.
goblet_squat.feel: Front of the thighs and glutes. Upper back and arms hold the weight.
avoid: Dumbbell drifting away from you. Keep it touching your chest.
Knees falling in. Push them out over your toes.

video.title: How to Perform Dumbbell Goblet Squat

good_morning.what: With a barbell on your upper back, you bow forward at the hips with a flat back and stand up again. It trains hamstrings and back.
good_morning.find: Squat rack with a barbell at upper chest height. Start with a light bar.
setup: Set the bar on your upper back as for a squat and step back.
Feet hip width, knees slightly bent, stomach tight.
do: Hinge at the hips: push your butt back and let your chest tip forward.
Keep your back flat and stop when the back of your thighs is stretched.
Push your hips forward to stand tall.
good_morning.feel: Back of the thighs, glutes and lower back.
avoid: Rounding your back. Go only as low as you can stay flat.
Loading it like a squat. Start very light and add weight slowly.

video.title: How To: Good Mornings

hack_squat.what: A squat on an angled sled machine with your back against a pad. It works the front thighs hard while your back is supported.
hack_squat.find: Angled machine with shoulder pads, a back pad and a foot plate. Plates load on the sides.
setup: Step in with your back flat on the pad and shoulders under the shoulder pads.
Feet shoulder width in the middle of the plate, toes slightly out.
Straighten your legs and turn the side handles to release the safety.
do: Lower slowly, knees following your toes, hips and back on the pad.
Go as deep as you can without your hips rolling off the pad.
Push through your whole foot until your legs are almost straight.
After the last rep, turn the handles back to lock the safety.
hack_squat.feel: Front of the thighs, with some glutes at the bottom.
avoid: Heels lifting. Move your feet a bit higher on the plate and keep heels down.
Snapping your knees locked at the top. Stop just short of locked.

video.title: Hack Squat | Exercise Guide

hammer_curl.what: A dumbbell curl with palms facing each other, like holding a hammer. It trains the biceps and the forearms.
setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs.
Pin your elbows to your sides.
do: Curl the dumbbells up with your thumbs pointing to the ceiling.
Stop when your thumbs are near your shoulders.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
hammer_curl.feel: Outside of the upper arms and top of the forearms.
avoid: Swinging your body. Stand still and use a weight you control.
Turning your palms up. Keep them facing each other all the way.

video.title: How To: Dumbbell Hammer Curl

hamstring_curl.what: Lying face down, you bend your knees to curl a padded roller toward your butt. It is direct work for the hamstrings.
hamstring_curl.find: Machine with a long pad to lie face down on and a padded roller behind the ankles.
setup: Adjust the roller so it sits just above your heels.
Lie face down with your knees just past the edge of the pad.
Hold the handles and press your hips into the pad.
do: Curl your heels toward your butt as far as you can.
Squeeze for a second at the top.
Lower slowly, about 3 seconds, until your legs are almost straight.
avoid: Hips lifting off the pad. Press them down and use less weight.
Letting the weight drop. Lower it slowly on every rep.

video.title: How to Lying Leg Curl | Proper Technique, Set Up, & Mistakes

hanging_knee_raise.what: Hanging from a bar, you lift your knees toward your chest. It trains your abs, mostly the lower part, and your grip.
hanging_knee_raise.find: A pull-up bar high enough that your feet clear the floor.
setup: Grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders, palms facing away.
Hang with straight arms and pull your shoulders slightly down.
Keep your legs together and your body still.
do: Bring your knees up toward your chest.
At the top, tilt your hips up so your lower back rounds a little.
Lower your legs slowly until they hang straight.
Stop any swing before the next rep.
hanging_knee_raise.feel: Lower stomach. Forearms and hands from hanging.
avoid: Swinging for momentum. Start each rep from a still hang.
Only lifting the thighs. Curl your hips up at the top to use your abs.

video.title: Hanging Knee Raise Tutorial - Proper Form and Technique

hanging_leg_raise.what: Hanging from a bar, you lift straight legs up in front of you. It is a harder version of the hanging knee raise for the abs.
hanging_leg_raise.find: A pull-up bar high enough that your feet clear the floor.
setup: Hang with straight arms, hands a bit wider than your shoulders.
Legs together and straight. Pull your shoulders slightly down.
do: Lift your legs in front of you until they are level with the floor.
Tilt your hips up at the top.
Lower slowly and stop any swing before the next rep.
hanging_leg_raise.feel: Lower stomach and the front of the hips. Your grip works too.
avoid: Swinging to throw the legs up. Start from a still hang and lift slowly.
Legs dropping fast. Lower them for 2 to 3 seconds.

video.title: How To: Hanging Leg-Lift

hip_thrust.what: With your upper back on a bench and a barbell over your hips, you drive your hips up. It is a main builder for the glutes.
hip_thrust.find: A flat bench, a barbell with big plates and a thick bar pad. Push the bench against a wall.
setup: Sit on the floor with your shoulder blades against the edge of the bench.
Roll the padded bar over your legs into the crease of your hips.
Feet flat and hip width, placed so your shins are upright at the top.
do: Tuck your chin and push through your heels to lift your hips.
Stop when your body is level from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes for a second, then lower under control.
avoid: Arching your lower back at the top. Keep ribs down and chin tucked.
Feet too far away or too close. Adjust until your shins are upright at the top.

video.title: How To Do a Barbell Hip Thrust
video.channel: Girls Gone Strong | Women's Health & Fitness

incline_bench_press.what: A barbell bench press on a bench tilted up. It puts more of the work on the upper chest and shoulders.
incline_bench_press.find: Incline bench with a barbell on uprights, or an adjustable bench inside a rack.
setup: Lie back with your eyes under the bar and feet flat.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and down.
Grip a little wider than shoulder width.
do: Lift the bar out and bring it over your shoulders.
Lower slowly to your upper chest, just below the collarbones.
Press straight up until your arms are straight.
incline_bench_press.feel: Upper chest and front of the shoulders, plus the back of the upper arms.
avoid: Lowering the bar to your stomach. Aim for the upper chest.
Hips lifting off the seat. Keep your butt down and feet planted.

video.title: How to PROPERLY Incline Barbell Bench Press (FIX YOUR FORM NOW)

incline_dumbbell_curl.what: A biceps curl lying back on an incline bench so your arms hang behind you. It works the biceps from a long stretch.
incline_dumbbell_curl.find: Adjustable bench set to about 45 to 60 degrees and two light dumbbells.
setup: Set the backrest to about 45 to 60 degrees and sit back against it.
Let your arms hang straight down, palms facing forward.
do: Curl the dumbbells up without letting your elbows move forward.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
incline_dumbbell_curl.feel: Front of the upper arms, with a stretch at the bottom.
avoid: Elbows swinging forward. Keep them pointing at the floor.
Head and shoulders lifting off the bench. Stay leaned back.

video.title: How To: Seated Incline Dumbbell Bicep Curl

incline_dumbbell_press.what: A dumbbell press on a bench tilted up about 30 degrees. It targets the upper chest and the front of the shoulders.
incline_dumbbell_press.find: Adjustable bench with the backrest raised about 30 degrees, and two dumbbells.
setup: Set the backrest to about 30 degrees. Steeper turns it into a shoulder press.
Sit with the dumbbells on your thighs, lie back and kick them up to your chest.
Feet flat on the floor, shoulder blades squeezed together.
do: Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight above your upper chest.
Lower slowly to the sides of your upper chest, elbows about 45 degrees out.
Press back up without banging the dumbbells together.
incline_dumbbell_press.feel: Upper chest just below the collarbones, and front of the shoulders.
avoid: Bench set too steep. Keep it near 30 degrees so your chest does the work.
Elbows flared wide. Tuck them slightly toward your sides.

video.title: How To: Dumbbell Incline Chest Press

incline_machine_press.what: A seated press machine where the handles travel up and forward. It trains the upper chest on a fixed, stable path.
incline_machine_press.find: Seated machine with a reclined backrest, marked Incline Press. Loaded with plates or a weight stack.
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your upper chest.
Sit back with your shoulder blades squeezed together against the pad.
Feet flat on the floor. Grip the handles with straight wrists.
do: Press the handles up and forward until your arms are almost straight.
Lower slowly until your hands are level with your chest.
Keep your shoulders back against the pad the whole time.
incline_machine_press.feel: Upper chest and front of the shoulders, plus the back of the upper arms.
avoid: Shoulders rolling forward at the top. Keep your shoulder blades pinned back.
Handles starting up by your neck. Raise the seat to upper chest height.

video.title: How To: Incline Chest Press (Hammer Strength)

inverted_row.what: Hanging under a bar with your heels on the floor, you pull your chest up to it. It is a bodyweight row for the back.
inverted_row.find: A barbell fixed in a rack or Smith machine at about waist height.
setup: Set the bar at waist height. Lower is harder, higher is easier.
Lie under it and grip a little wider than your shoulders, palms facing away.
Straighten your body with heels on the floor and arms straight.
do: Squeeze your glutes so your body stays straight like a plank.
Pull your chest up to the bar, elbows going back.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
inverted_row.feel: Middle of the back between the shoulder blades, plus the front of the arms.
avoid: Hips sagging. Keep a straight line from heels to head.
Stopping short. Touch your chest to the bar, or raise the bar a notch.

video.title: How To PROPERLY Inverted Row For Muscle Gain

kettlebell_swing.what: You swing a kettlebell from between your legs to chest height with a fast hip snap. It builds power in glutes and hamstrings.
kettlebell_swing.find: A kettlebell, a ball shaped weight with a handle. Keep the space in front of you clear.
setup: Stand with feet a bit wider than your shoulders, the bell 30 cm in front.
Push your hips back with a flat back and grip the handle with both hands.
Tilt the bell toward you and pull your shoulders down.
do: Hike the bell back between your legs, forearms against your inner thighs.
Snap your hips forward and stand tall. The bell floats to chest height.
Let it fall, and fold at the hips only when your arms reach your body.
kettlebell_swing.feel: Glutes and back of the thighs. Your arms only guide the bell.
avoid: Squatting and lifting with the arms. Push hips back, then snap them forward.
Leaning back at the top. Finish standing tall with glutes tight.

video.title: How To Kettlebell Swing (in 3 minutes)

landmine_press.what: You press one end of a barbell up and forward while the other end is anchored to the floor. The angled path suits most shoulders.
landmine_press.find: A barbell with one end in a floor pivot (landmine) or wedged in a corner. Plates go on the free end.
setup: Load the free end and lift it to one shoulder with both hands.
Hold the end of the bar in one hand at shoulder height, elbow tucked.
Stand with one foot in front, or kneel on the knee of the pressing side.
do: Press the bar up and forward until your arm is straight.
Let your shoulder reach forward a little at the top.
Lower slowly back to your shoulder.
Finish all reps, then switch sides.
landmine_press.feel: Front of the shoulder and upper chest, plus the back of the upper arm.
avoid: Leaning back. Keep your ribs down and lean slightly into the bar.
Twisting your upper body. Keep hips and chest square to the bar.

video.title: Landmine Press for Shoulder health (DO THEM NOW)

lat_pulldown.what: Seated, you pull a wide bar down to your upper chest. It builds the big back muscles you use in pull-ups.
lat_pulldown.find: Seated cable machine with a long bar hanging overhead and pads that hold your thighs down.
setup: Adjust the thigh pads so they hold your legs down firmly.
Stand up and grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders, palms away.
Sit down with the bar and lean back just slightly, chest up.
do: Pull your shoulders down first, then drive your elbows down to your sides.
Bring the bar to your upper chest.
Let it rise slowly until your arms are straight and your sides stretch.
lat_pulldown.feel: The sides of your back under the armpits, plus the front of your upper arms.
avoid: Leaning far back and yanking. Stay nearly upright and use less weight.
Pulling the bar behind your neck. Always pull to the front of your chest.

video.title: How to do the LAT PULLDOWN! | 2 Minute Tutorial

lateral_raise.what: You lift light dumbbells out to your sides to shoulder height. It builds the side of the shoulders.
lateral_raise.find: A pair of light dumbbells. Start lighter than you think.
setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Bend your elbows slightly and lean forward just a touch.
do: Lift your arms out to the sides, leading with your elbows.
Stop when your hands reach shoulder height.
Lower slowly, 2 to 3 seconds.
avoid: Swinging the weights up with your body. Go lighter and stand still.
Shrugging toward your ears. Keep your shoulders down as you lift.

video.title: How To: Dumbbell Side Lateral Raise

leg_extension.what: Seated, you straighten your knees against a padded roller. It isolates the front of the thighs.
leg_extension.find: Seated machine with a padded roller in front of your shins and a weight stack.
setup: Adjust the backrest so your knees line up with the pivot of the machine.
Set the roller so it rests just above your ankles.
Sit back and hold the side handles.
do: Straighten your legs fully.
Squeeze your thighs for a second at the top.
Lower slowly, about 3 seconds.
leg_extension.feel: Front of the thighs, just above the knees.
avoid: Kicking the weight up. Lift smoothly and pause at the top.
Butt lifting off the seat. Hold the handles and stay seated.

video.title: How To: Leg Extension (Cybex)

leg_press.what: Seated in a machine, you push a weighted platform away with your legs. It builds thighs and glutes with your back supported.
leg_press.find: Large machine with a reclined seat and a big foot platform, often angled up at 45 degrees.
setup: Sit with your hips and back flat against the pad.
Feet shoulder width in the middle of the platform, toes slightly out.
Push the platform up a little and turn the side handles to release it.
do: Lower slowly until your knees are bent to about 90 degrees.
Keep your hips and lower back on the pad at the bottom.
Push through your whole foot until your legs are almost straight.
After the last rep, lock the safety handles before you relax.
leg_press.feel: Front of the thighs and glutes.
avoid: Hips curling off the seat at the bottom. Stop a little higher.
Locking the knees hard at the top. Stop just short of straight.

video.title: How to PROPERLY Leg Press (FIX YOUR FORM NOW)

machine_chest_press.what: Seated, you push two handles straight forward from your chest. It is a stable way to train chest, shoulders and triceps.
machine_chest_press.find: Seated machine marked Chest Press, with an upright backrest and handles at chest height.
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles are level with the middle of your chest.
Sit back with your shoulder blades squeezed together against the pad.
Feet flat. Grip the handles with straight wrists.
do: Press the handles forward until your arms are almost straight.
Return slowly until your hands are beside your chest.
Keep your shoulders back against the pad.
machine_chest_press.feel: Chest, front of the shoulders and back of the upper arms.
avoid: Shoulders rounding forward. Keep your chest up and shoulder blades back.
Handles up at shoulder height. Raise the seat until they line up with mid chest.

video.title: How to Use the Chest Press Machine (Proper Form)

machine_crunch.what: Seated in a machine, you curl your chest down toward your hips against resistance. It is a simple way to add weight to ab work.
machine_crunch.find: Seated machine marked Abdominal or Ab Crunch, with handles or pads by your shoulders.
setup: Pick a light weight and set the seat so the pads sit at your upper chest.
Hook your feet under the foot pads if the machine has them.
Hold the handles lightly.
do: Curl your ribs down toward your hips by rounding your back.
Squeeze your abs for a second.
Return slowly until you are upright again.
avoid: Pulling with your arms. Keep them relaxed and curl with your abs.
Folding at the hips with a straight back. Round your spine as you crunch.

video.title: How To: Abdominal Crunch (Hammer Strength)

machine_row.what: Seated with your chest against a pad, you pull two handles toward your body. It trains the upper back with full support.
machine_row.find: Seated row machine with a chest pad and handles in front. Weight stack or plates.
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles are at lower chest height.
Set the chest pad so you can just reach the handles with straight arms.
Sit tall with your chest on the pad and feet flat.
do: Pull the handles back, driving your elbows past your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for a second.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.
machine_row.feel: Middle of the back between the shoulder blades, plus the front of the arms.
avoid: Chest coming off the pad. Stay against it and use less weight.
Shrugging up. Keep your shoulders low and pull your elbows back.

video.title: How To Use The Seated Row Machine

machine_shoulder_press.what: Seated, you push two handles from shoulder height to overhead. It is a stable way to build the shoulders.
machine_shoulder_press.find: Seated machine marked Shoulder Press, with handles beside your shoulders.
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Sit back against the pad with your feet flat.
Grip the handles with your elbows under your wrists.
do: Press up until your arms are almost straight.
Lower slowly back to shoulder height.
Keep your back against the pad the whole time.
machine_shoulder_press.feel: Shoulders and back of the upper arms.
avoid: Arching away from the backrest. Keep ribs down and back on the pad.
Short reps at the top. Lower all the way to shoulder height.

video.title: How to PROPERLY Shoulder Machine Press (LEARN FAST)

neutral_grip_pulldown.what: A lat pulldown with palms facing each other on a narrow handle. It is comfortable for the shoulders and works the back hard.
neutral_grip_pulldown.find: Lat pulldown machine with a V shaped handle or a bar with parallel grips.
setup: Clip on the V handle and set the thigh pads snug.
Grip with palms facing each other and sit down with straight arms.
Lean back slightly with your chest up.
do: Pull the handle down to your upper chest, elbows close to your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades down and together.
Let it rise slowly until your arms are straight.
neutral_grip_pulldown.feel: The sides of your back under the armpits, plus the front of your upper arms.
avoid: Rocking back to move the weight. Stay nearly upright.
Stopping short at the top. Let your arms stretch fully on each rep.

video.title: Neutral Grip Pulldowns [Perfect Form in 60 Seconds]

nordic_curl.what: Kneeling with your ankles held down, you lower your body forward as slowly as you can. It builds very strong hamstrings.
nordic_curl.find: A knee pad and something solid to hook your heels under, or a partner to hold your ankles.
setup: Kneel on a pad and lock your heels under something solid that will not move.
Body straight from knees to head, hands ready in front of your chest.
do: Squeeze your glutes and lean forward slowly from the knees.
Fight the fall for as long as you can, 3 to 5 seconds.
Catch yourself with your hands, then push off the floor to get back up.
nordic_curl.feel: Back of the thighs, working very hard.
avoid: Bending at the hips. Keep knees, hips and shoulders in one line.
Dropping fast. Lower only as far as you can control, then use your hands.

video.title: Nordic Hamstring Curls for Beginners (In 1 Minute!)

one_arm_dumbbell_row.what: With one hand and one knee on a bench, you pull a dumbbell up to your side. It trains the back one side at a time.
one_arm_dumbbell_row.find: A flat bench and one dumbbell.
setup: Put your left knee and left hand on the bench, right foot on the floor.
Flatten your back so it is roughly level with the floor.
Pick up the dumbbell in your right hand and let the arm hang straight.
do: Pull the dumbbell up toward your hip, elbow close to your side.
Squeeze your shoulder blade back at the top.
Lower slowly until your arm is straight.
Finish all reps, then switch sides.
one_arm_dumbbell_row.feel: The side and middle of your back on the working side.
avoid: Twisting your body open to lift. Keep both shoulders level with the floor.
Yanking with the arm. Think of pulling your elbow to your back pocket.

video.title: How To: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row (Single-Arm)

overhead_press.what: Standing, you press a barbell from your collarbones to straight overhead. It is the main lift for strong shoulders.
overhead_press.find: A barbell in a squat rack with the hooks set at upper chest height.
setup: Grip the bar just wider than your shoulders and step under it.
Rest the bar on your collarbones, elbows slightly in front of the bar.
Step back. Feet hip width, glutes and stomach tight.
do: Press the bar straight up, pulling your chin back to let it pass your face.
Once it passes your forehead, move your head forward under the bar.
Finish with arms straight and the bar over the middle of your feet.
Lower under control to your collarbones.
overhead_press.feel: Shoulders and back of the upper arms. Your stomach holds you stiff.
avoid: Leaning back to press. Squeeze your glutes and keep your ribs down.
Pushing with your legs. Keep your knees straight and still.

video.title: How To: Standing Straight-Bar Military / Overhead Press

overhead_triceps_extension.what: You hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands and lower it behind your head. It trains the triceps in a deep stretch.
overhead_triceps_extension.find: One dumbbell. Stand, or sit on a bench with a short backrest.
setup: Hold one dumbbell upright with both hands cupped under the top end.
Lift it overhead until your arms are straight.
Keep your ribs down and your stomach tight.
do: Bend your elbows and lower the dumbbell slowly behind your head.
Keep your upper arms still and close to your head.
Straighten your arms to lift the dumbbell back overhead.
overhead_triceps_extension.feel: Back of the upper arms, with a stretch at the bottom.
avoid: Elbows flaring far out. Keep them pointing forward, close to your head.
Arching your lower back. Tighten your abs or sit against a backrest.

video.title: How To: Standing Overhead Dumbbell Tricep Extension

pallof_press.what: Standing side on to a cable, you press the handle straight out and resist being twisted. It trains your abs to stop rotation.
pallof_press.find: Cable tower with a single handle, pulley set at chest height.
setup: Set the pulley at chest height and stand side on to the tower.
Hold the handle at your chest with both hands and step out until the weight lifts.
Feet shoulder width, knees soft, stomach tight.
do: Press your hands straight out in front of your chest.
Hold for 2 seconds. Do not let the cable turn you toward the tower.
Bring your hands back to your chest.
Finish all reps, then face the other way.
pallof_press.feel: The sides of your stomach, working to stop you from twisting.
avoid: Hips or shoulders turning. Keep both facing straight ahead.
Too much weight. Go light enough to stay completely still.

video.title: How to Do the Pallof Press (Perfect Form for a Stronger Core)

pec_deck.what: Seated, you bring the two arms of the machine together in front of your chest. It isolates the chest on a fixed path.
pec_deck.find: Seated machine with two swinging arms, marked Pec Fly, Pec Deck or Butterfly.
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height.
Set the arms so the start position gives a light chest stretch.
Sit back with your chest up and elbows slightly bent.
do: Bring the handles together in front of your chest in a wide arc.
Squeeze your chest for a second.
Open slowly until you feel a stretch across the chest.
pec_deck.feel: Across the chest, most in the middle when your hands meet.
avoid: Shoulders rolling forward. Keep your shoulder blades back against the pad.
Letting the weight yank your arms back. Open under control.

video.title: The Chest PEC DEC FLY | Exercise Form Guide

plank.what: You hold your body straight on your forearms and toes. It trains your abs to keep your trunk stiff.
plank.find: A mat on the floor. No equipment needed.
setup: Forearms on the floor, elbows right under your shoulders.
Step your feet back so you rest on your toes with straight legs.
do: Make one straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and tighten your stomach as if bracing for a poke.
Breathe normally and hold for the set time.
plank.feel: The front of your stomach, plus shoulders and glutes.
avoid: Hips sagging. Squeeze your glutes and tuck your tailbone slightly.
Hips piked high. Lower them until shoulders, hips and heels line up.

video.title: Mastering the Plank - In Just 2 Minutes

pull_up.what: Hanging from a bar, you pull yourself up until your chin is over it. It is the classic bodyweight builder for back and arms.
pull_up.find: A pull-up bar. Use a box or step to reach it if needed.
setup: Grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders, palms facing away.
Hang with straight arms and keep your legs together.
Tighten your stomach so your body does not swing.
do: Pull your shoulders down away from your ears first.
Drive your elbows down to your sides until your chin clears the bar.
Lower slowly, 2 to 3 seconds, to fully straight arms.
pull_up.feel: The sides of your back under the armpits, plus upper arms and forearms.
avoid: Kicking or swinging. Keep your legs still and pull smoothly.
Half reps. Go from straight arms to chin over the bar every time.

video.title: The Perfect Pull Up  - Do it right!

push_up.what: With hands and toes on the floor, you lower your chest and push back up. It builds chest, shoulders and triceps.
push_up.find: Open floor space. A mat is optional.
setup: Hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders, fingers forward.
Step your feet back. Body in a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and tighten your stomach.
do: Lower your chest toward the floor, elbows about 45 degrees from your sides.
Go down until your chest is just above the floor.
Push the floor away until your arms are straight.
push_up.feel: Chest, front of the shoulders and back of the upper arms.
avoid: Hips sagging or sticking up. Hold one straight line, like a moving plank.
Elbows flared straight out. Point them back at about 45 degrees.

video.title: The Perfect Push Up | Do it right!

rear_delt_machine.what: Facing the pad of a fly machine, you sweep your arms out and back. It isolates the back of the shoulders.
rear_delt_machine.find: The pec fly machine used backwards. Sit facing the pad with the handles set to the rear position.
setup: Move the arms of the machine to the rearmost setting.
Sit facing the pad with your chest against it, handles at shoulder height.
Grip with your arms long in front of you, elbows slightly bent.
do: Sweep your arms out and back in a wide arc.
Stop when your arms are in line with your shoulders.
Return slowly without letting the weight touch down.
avoid: Bending your elbows and rowing. Keep your arms long and sweep wide.
Chest leaving the pad. Stay against it and reduce the weight.

video.title: How to PROPERLY Reverse Pec Deck Fly (DO THIS)

reverse_fly.what: Lying chest down on an incline bench, you lift light dumbbells out to the sides. It trains the back of the shoulders.
reverse_fly.find: Adjustable bench set to a low incline and two light dumbbells.
setup: Set the bench to about 30 to 45 degrees.
Lie chest down, feet on the floor, a light dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang down, palms facing each other, elbows slightly bent.
do: Lift your arms out to the sides in a wide arc.
Stop when your arms are level with your shoulders.
Pause, then lower slowly. Keep the same slight elbow bend.
reverse_fly.feel: Back of the shoulders and between the shoulder blades.
avoid: Going heavy and jerking. Pick a weight you can pause with at the top.
Bending the elbows into a row. Keep your arms long and sweep wide.

video.title: How to: Prone Dumbbell Rear Delt Fly

reverse_lunge.what: Holding dumbbells, you step one foot back into a lunge and return to standing. It builds legs and glutes and is easy to balance.
reverse_lunge.find: Two dumbbells and a little floor space.
setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, feet hip width.
Tighten your stomach and look straight ahead.
do: Take a long step straight back and land on the ball of that foot.
Lower until your back knee is just above the floor.
Push through the front foot to stand up and bring the back foot forward.
Do all reps on one leg, or alternate legs.
reverse_lunge.feel: Thigh and glute of the front leg.
avoid: Pushing off the back foot. Keep your weight on the front leg.
Feet in one line. Step back with your feet hip width apart.

video.title: How To: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge

romanian_deadlift.what: Holding a barbell, you push your hips back and lower the bar along your legs with a flat back. It builds hamstrings and glutes.
romanian_deadlift.find: A barbell, ideally taken from a rack at mid thigh height. Otherwise lift it from the floor.
setup: Grip the bar at shoulder width, palms facing you, and stand up tall with it.
Feet hip width, knees slightly bent.
Pull your shoulders back and tighten your stomach.
do: Hinge at the hips: push your butt straight back, knees only slightly bent.
Slide the bar down your thighs with a flat back.
Stop just below the knees or when the back of your thighs is fully stretched.
Push your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand tall.
romanian_deadlift.feel: A deep stretch in the back of the thighs, then glutes on the way up.
avoid: Bar drifting away from your legs. Keep it brushing your thighs.
Rounding your back to go lower. Stop where your back stays flat.

video.title: How to do the ROMANIAN DEADLIFT! | 2 Minute Tutorial

seated_cable_row.what: Seated at a low cable, you pull a handle to your stomach. It builds the middle of the back and the muscles that pull your shoulders back.
seated_cable_row.find: Low cable with a bench seat and foot plates, usually with a V shaped double handle.
setup: Sit on the bench with your feet on the foot plates, knees slightly bent.
Grab the handle and slide back until your arms are straight.
Sit tall with your chest up and back flat.
do: Pull the handle to your lower ribs, elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for a second.
Return slowly until your arms are straight. Stay tall.
seated_cable_row.feel: Middle of your back between the shoulder blades, plus the front of the arms.
avoid: Rocking back and forth. Keep your upper body almost still and upright.
Rounding forward on the way out. Keep your chest up.

video.title: Seated Cable Row | Exercise Guide

seated_calf_raise.what: Seated with pads on your knees, you lift your heels as high as you can. It trains the deep muscle of the calf.
seated_calf_raise.find: Low seated machine with knee pads and a foot bar. Plates load on a lever in front.
setup: Sit with the balls of your feet on the foot bar, heels hanging off.
Slide the pads snug onto your lower thighs, just above the knees.
Lift your heels a little and move the safety lever aside.
do: Lower your heels slowly until you feel a deep calf stretch.
Push up onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Pause for a second at the top and at the bottom.
seated_calf_raise.feel: Calves, low on the back of the lower leg.
avoid: Bouncing quickly. Pause at the bottom and top of every rep.
Half reps. Go all the way down and all the way up.

seated_dumbbell_press.what: Seated with back support, you press two dumbbells overhead. It builds the shoulders while the bench keeps your back steady.
seated_dumbbell_press.find: Adjustable bench with the backrest nearly upright, and two dumbbells.
setup: Set the backrest one notch back from fully upright.
Sit down, dumbbells on your thighs, then kick them up to your shoulders.
Palms forward, elbows under your wrists and slightly in front of you.
do: Press both dumbbells up until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly until the dumbbells are about level with your ears.
Keep your back and head against the backrest.
seated_dumbbell_press.feel: Shoulders and back of the upper arms.
avoid: Arching hard off the backrest. Keep your ribs down and feet planted.
Stopping high. Lower until your hands are about ear level.

video.title: How to do the SEATED DUMBBELL SHOULDER PRESS! | 2 Minute Tutorial

seated_leg_curl.what: Seated, you bend your knees to pull a padded roller down and under you. It trains the hamstrings.
seated_leg_curl.find: Seated machine with a roller behind your ankles and a pad that clamps over your thighs.
setup: Adjust the backrest so your knees line up with the pivot of the machine.
Rest your legs on the roller so it sits just above your heels.
Lower the thigh pad firmly onto your thighs, just above the knees.
do: Pull your heels down and back under the seat as far as you can.
Squeeze for a second.
Let the roller rise slowly, about 3 seconds, until your legs are almost straight.
avoid: Letting the weight snap back. Control the way up.
Hips sliding forward. Sit back and keep the thigh pad tight.

side_plank.what: Lying on your side, you hold your body straight on one forearm and the side of your foot. It trains the side abs.
side_plank.find: A mat on the floor. No equipment needed.
setup: Lie on your side with your elbow right under your shoulder.
Legs straight, feet stacked on top of each other.
do: Lift your hips until your body is a straight line from head to feet.
Push the floor away with your forearm and squeeze your glutes.
Hold for the set time, then switch sides.
side_plank.feel: The side of your stomach closest to the floor, plus the shoulder.
avoid: Hips sagging or drifting back. Push them up and forward into a straight line.
Losing position early. Bend your knees and hold from your knees.

single_arm_dumbbell_bench_press.what: A flat dumbbell bench press with one arm at a time. Your trunk has to work to keep you level on the bench.
single_arm_dumbbell_bench_press.find: A flat bench and one dumbbell.
setup: Lie on the bench with one dumbbell held at the side of your chest.
Plant both feet wide on the floor and tighten your stomach.
Rest the free hand on your stomach or hold it out to the side.
do: Press the dumbbell up until your arm is straight over your shoulder.
Lower slowly to the side of your chest, elbow about 45 degrees out.
Finish all reps, then switch arms.
single_arm_dumbbell_bench_press.feel: Chest and back of the arm on the working side. Abs keep you level.
avoid: Body twisting toward the weight. Press your feet down and keep hips level.
Starting as heavy as with two dumbbells. Begin lighter.

video.title: Single Arm Dumbbell Chest Press Exercise Tutorial

single_arm_dumbbell_shoulder_press.what: A dumbbell overhead press with one arm at a time. It builds each shoulder separately and makes your trunk hold steady.
single_arm_dumbbell_shoulder_press.find: One dumbbell. Stand, or sit on a bench with an upright backrest.
setup: Bring one dumbbell to shoulder height, palm facing forward.
Feet hip width, glutes and stomach tight.
Rest the free hand on your hip or hold it out to the side.
do: Press the dumbbell straight up until your arm is straight beside your ear.
Lower slowly back to your shoulder.
Finish all reps, then switch arms.
single_arm_dumbbell_shoulder_press.feel: Shoulder and back of the working arm. Side abs hold you upright.
avoid: Leaning away from the weight. Stay tall with level shoulders.
Arching your back. Squeeze your glutes and keep your ribs down.

single_arm_pulldown.what: A lat pulldown with one arm and a single handle. It lets each side of your back work on its own through a long range.
single_arm_pulldown.find: Lat pulldown machine or high cable with a single D shaped handle.
setup: Clip a single handle to the high cable.
Grip it with one hand and sit down with your thighs under the pads.
Arm straight overhead, chest up.
do: Pull your elbow down to your side, toward your hip.
Squeeze your back for a second.
Let the handle rise slowly until your arm is straight and your side stretches.
Finish all reps, then switch arms.
single_arm_pulldown.feel: The side of your back under the armpit on the working side.
avoid: Leaning far to the side to pull. Stay tall and move the arm.
Curling with the biceps. Think about driving your elbow to your hip.

single_leg_rdl.what: Standing on one leg, you tip forward with a flat back while the other leg reaches behind. It trains hamstrings, glutes and balance.
single_leg_rdl.find: One dumbbell or kettlebell and a little floor space. A wall or rack to touch helps at first.
setup: Stand on one leg with that knee slightly bent.
Hold the dumbbell in the hand opposite the standing leg.
do: Hinge at the hips: push your butt back and tip your chest forward.
Let the free leg rise straight behind you, hips level with the floor.
Lower until your back is near level or the back of your thigh is stretched.
Push your hip forward to stand. Finish all reps, then switch legs.
single_leg_rdl.feel: Back of the thigh and glute of the standing leg.
avoid: Hip opening to the side. Point the toes of the back foot at the floor.
Rounding your back to reach the floor. Stop where your back stays flat.

skull_crusher.what: Lying on a bench, you lower a bar toward your forehead by bending your elbows, then straighten them. It works the triceps.
skull_crusher.find: A flat bench and a short zigzag bar, called an EZ bar.
setup: Lie on the bench holding the bar over your chest with straight arms.
Grip the inner angled parts, hands about shoulder width, palms toward your feet.
Tilt your arms slightly back toward your head.
do: Bend only your elbows and lower the bar slowly to your forehead.
Keep your upper arms still and elbows pointing up.
Straighten your arms back to the start.
avoid: Elbows flaring out wide. Keep them shoulder width apart.
Upper arms rocking. Hold them still so only the forearms move.

smith_machine_squat.what: A squat with a bar that slides on fixed rails. The machine handles the balance so you can focus on your legs.
smith_machine_squat.find: A rack where the bar runs on vertical rails and hooks on with a twist of the wrists.
setup: Set the bar at upper chest height and the safety stops below squat depth.
Stand under the bar with it on your upper back, feet slightly in front of it.
Lift and roll your wrists to unhook the bar.
do: Take a breath, tighten your stomach and sit down under control.
Go until your thighs are level with the floor.
Push through your whole foot to stand up.
After the last rep, roll your wrists to hook the bar back on.
smith_machine_squat.feel: Front of the thighs and glutes.
avoid: Heels lifting. Move your feet a little forward and keep them flat.
Knees caving in. Push them out over your toes.

split_squat.what: A lunge held in place. One foot forward, one back, and you go straight down and up. It builds each leg and your balance.
split_squat.find: Two dumbbells and a little floor space. A mat under the back knee is nice.
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Take a long step forward. Keep your feet hip width apart, as if on rails.
Lift your back heel and put most of your weight on the front foot.
do: Bend both knees and lower straight down.
Stop when your back knee is just above the floor.
Push through the whole front foot to stand up. Your feet stay in place.
Finish all reps, then switch legs.
split_squat.feel: Front thigh and glute of the front leg.
avoid: Feet in one line like on a tightrope. Keep them hip width apart.
Front heel lifting. Take a longer stance and keep the whole foot down.

standing_calf_raise.what: Standing with pads on your shoulders, you rise up on your toes and lower your heels. It builds the calves.
standing_calf_raise.find: Upright machine with shoulder pads and a step for the balls of your feet.
setup: Adjust the pads so you must bend your knees slightly to get under them.
Stand with the balls of your feet on the step, heels hanging off.
Straighten your legs to lift the weight.
do: Lower your heels slowly until you feel a deep calf stretch.
Pause, then rise as high as you can onto the balls of your feet.
Squeeze for a second at the top.
standing_calf_raise.feel: Calves, high on the back of the lower leg.
avoid: Bouncing at the bottom. Pause in the stretch before each rise.
Bending your knees to help. Keep your legs straight but not locked.

step_up.what: Holding dumbbells, you step up onto a box with one leg and come down slowly. It builds each leg and hip on its own.
step_up.find: A sturdy box or bench about knee height, and two dumbbells.
setup: Stand facing the box with a dumbbell in each hand.
Place your whole foot on the box, heel included.
do: Lean slightly forward and push through the top foot to stand on the box.
Let the top leg do the work. Do not spring off the bottom foot.
Lower yourself slowly, 2 to 3 seconds, until the other foot touches down.
Finish all reps on one leg, then switch.
step_up.feel: Thigh and glute of the leg on the box.
avoid: Bouncing off the floor foot. Tap the floor lightly and push with the top leg.
Knee caving inward. Keep it pointing over your toes.

straight_arm_pulldown.what: Standing at a high cable, you sweep a bar down to your thighs with straight arms. It isolates the big muscles on the sides of your back.
straight_arm_pulldown.find: Cable tower with the pulley at the top and a straight bar or rope.
setup: Set the pulley high and grip the bar palms down at shoulder width.
Step back so your arms reach up and forward with the weight lifted.
Lean forward slightly from the hips with soft knees.
do: With arms almost straight, sweep the bar down in an arc to your thighs.
Squeeze the sides of your back for a second.
Let the bar rise slowly until your hands are above head height.
straight_arm_pulldown.feel: The sides of your back under the armpits.
avoid: Bending the elbows and pushing down with the arms. Keep your arms long.
Rocking your body. Hold your lean and move only at the shoulders.

suitcase_carry.what: You walk holding one heavy dumbbell in one hand, like a suitcase. Your side abs have to work to keep you upright.
suitcase_carry.find: One heavy dumbbell or kettlebell and a clear lane of 10 to 20 metres.
setup: Stand beside the dumbbell. Bend knees and hips to grip it, back flat.
Stand up tall with the weight hanging at your side.
Level your shoulders. Keep the free arm relaxed.
do: Walk with short, steady steps and look straight ahead.
Stay upright. Do not lean toward the weight or away from it.
Set it down with a flat back, switch hands and walk back.
suitcase_carry.feel: The side of your stomach opposite the weight, plus hand and forearm.
avoid: Leaning away from the weight. Stand tall with level shoulders and hips.
Resting the weight on your leg. Hold it just clear of your thigh.

sumo_deadlift.what: A deadlift with a very wide stance and your hands inside your knees. Your upper body stays more upright than in a regular deadlift.
sumo_deadlift.find: A barbell with full size plates on the floor, on a lifting platform or rubber mats.
setup: Stand wide with toes turned out and shins close to the bar.
Push your knees out and reach straight down to grip the bar at shoulder width.
Lift your chest, flatten your back and pull up until the bar feels tight.
do: Take a big breath and tighten your stomach.
Push the floor apart with your feet and stand up with the bar close.
Stand tall and squeeze your glutes. Do not lean back.
Lower under control along the same path.
sumo_deadlift.feel: Glutes, inner thighs and front of the thighs, plus your back.
avoid: Knees falling inward. Keep pushing them out over your toes.
Hips shooting up first. Lift chest and hips at the same speed.

video.title: How To Correctly Perform A Sumo Deadlift

t_bar_row.what: Bent over a barbell that is anchored at one end, you row the loaded end up toward your chest. It builds a thick, strong back.
t_bar_row.find: A barbell in a floor pivot (landmine) or corner, plates on the free end and a V handle.
setup: Stand over the bar facing the loaded end and hook a V handle under it.
Push your hips back, bend your knees and grip the handle with a flat back.
Lift the plates off the floor. Chest up, back at about 45 degrees.
do: Pull the handle to your upper stomach, elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight. Keep your upper body still.
t_bar_row.feel: Middle and sides of the back, plus the front of the arms.
avoid: Jerking upright to move the weight. Hold your lean and go lighter.
Rounding your back. Keep your chest up and back flat.

trap_bar_deadlift.what: You stand inside a six sided bar and lift it from the floor with handles at your sides. It is a deadlift that is easier to learn.
trap_bar_deadlift.find: A six sided bar you step into, with a handle on each side. Also called a hex bar.
setup: Step inside the bar with feet hip width, centred between the plates.
Push your hips back, bend your knees and grip the middle of the handles.
Lift your chest, flatten your back and pull up until the bar feels tight.
do: Take a big breath and tighten your stomach.
Push the floor away and stand up tall with straight arms.
Stand straight at the top. Do not lean back.
Lower under control by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
trap_bar_deadlift.feel: Glutes, thighs and back. Your grip works too.
avoid: Rounding your back. Chest up and back flat before the bar leaves the floor.
Yanking the bar. Squeeze it up smoothly from a tight start.

video.title: How to Do a Trap Bar Deadlift

triceps_pushdown.what: Standing at a high cable, you push a bar down by straightening your elbows. It is direct work for the triceps.
triceps_pushdown.find: Cable tower with the pulley at the top and a short straight or angled bar, or a rope.
setup: Set the pulley high and clip on a short bar.
Grip it palms down, hands shoulder width, and pull it down to chest height.
Stand close with a slight forward lean, elbows pinned to your sides.
do: Push the bar down until your arms are fully straight.
Squeeze the back of your arms for a second.
Let the bar rise slowly until your forearms are just above level.
avoid: Elbows swinging forward and back. Keep them fixed at your sides.
Leaning your body weight onto the bar. Stay tall and go lighter.

walking_lunge.what: Holding dumbbells, you take long steps forward and drop into a lunge with each step. It builds legs, glutes and balance.
walking_lunge.find: Two dumbbells and a clear lane about 10 metres long.
setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Look ahead and tighten your stomach.
do: Take a long step forward and lower until your back knee is just above the floor.
Keep your front foot flat and your chest up.
Push through the front foot and bring the back leg through into the next step.
Keep alternating legs down the lane.
walking_lunge.feel: Thighs and glutes of both legs, mostly the front leg on each step.
avoid: Short, choppy steps. Step long enough that the front heel stays down.
Back knee slamming the floor. Lower under control and stop just above it.
